intro: An L1 penalty can set coefficients exactly to zero. Its proximal update shrinks each magnitude by a fixed amount without changing the sign of surviving values.
task: Apply the elementwise proximal operator of threshold times the L1 norm to a vector.
requirements: values is a nonempty vector and threshold is a scalar in [0,1e6].
Return sign(values)*maximum(abs(values)-threshold,0) as a new NumPy vector.
Values whose magnitude is at most threshold become zero. This is soft thresholding, not hard deletion of only the smallest entries.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Separate sign and magnitude so shrinking a positive value and shrinking a negative value follow the same rule.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Subtract the threshold from magnitudes, clip at zero, then restore the original signs.

explanation: For a scalar input x, minimizing one half of (z-x)^2 plus threshold*abs(z) gives a signed shrinkage rule. The penalty wins completely when the input magnitude is below the threshold.
Hard thresholding would leave retained values untouched. Soft thresholding also moves every retained coefficient toward zero, which matters when combining this operator with gradient steps.
